## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vakkalittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 534) is a Pali verse narrative included in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the past karmic background and spiritual biography of the elder Vakkali. While SuttaCentral records five modern translations in five languages, it lists no curated parallels in other Buddhist traditions [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus shows extensive sharing of material within Pali literature, identifying 222 matching passages across 57 texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest concentration of text reuse is with the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Dutiyo bhāgo), where a long sequence spanning segments 13.4–34.4 matches segments 789–831 of the commentary (over 6,300 characters, 0.88 similarity), with additional matches in the first volume of the commentary and the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Conventional formulaic verses are shared with multiple other apadānas of monks and nuns, most notably the *Mahākoṭṭhikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 539), *Kaṅkhārevatattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 544), *Sīvalittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 545), *Rādhattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 541), *Sakulātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 24), and *Kāḷudāyittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 548) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated matches, DharmaNexus identifies alignments with the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* de Subaši (best score 65), as well as Tibetan versions of the *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* and the *Arthaviniścayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
